# odyssey-003 (1.213–324) — new fixed renderings

These are formulas and epithets that will plainly recur and that the house table in `conventions.md` does
not yet cover. Nothing here changes an existing table entry. The following are taken from the table or
from odyssey-001/002 as they stand: γλαυκῶπις Ἀθήνη (221, 314, 319), τὸν δ’ αὖτε προσέειπε (221),
τὸν δ’ ἠμείβετ’ ἔπειτα (314), ἀλλ’ ἄγε μοι τόδε εἰπὲ … (224), ὢ πόποι (253), ἀμύμων (232, of a house),
ὑλήεις (246), δῖος (Nestor 284, Orestes 298, kept as "heavenly"), φίλη πατρὶς γαῖα (290, rendered like
φίλη πατρὶς αἶα), Παλλὰς Ἀθήνη (252) and ξεῖνοι as "guest-friends" (313, as at 1.187).

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| τὴν δ’ αὖ Τηλέμαχος πεπνυμένος ἀντίον ηὔδα (213, 230, 306) | "To her in turn prudent Telemachus spoke, face to face:" | "Then prudent Telemachus spoke to her in turn, face to face:" | "answered" (reserved for ἠμείβετο), "addressed" (already used for προσέειπε / προσέφη) |

The fourth reply-formula. ἀντίον ηὔδα is "spoke face to face" (ἀντίον is an adverb of facing), so it is kept apart from the three that are already fixed.

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| πεπνυμένος (of Telemachus) | "prudent" | "prudent" | "thoughtful", "clear-headed", "poised", "sensible", anything in "-minded" (kept for the -φρων epithets) |

This is the perfect participle of πέπνυμαι, 'have one's wits about one'. The link with πνέω is traditional and uncertain, and the note says so. "Prudent" is the plain lexicon sense, and it is not a φρήν-compound.

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| θεοὶ αἰὲν ἐόντες (263) | "the gods who are forever" | "the gods who are forever" | "the immortal gods" (that is ἀθάνατοι), "the everlasting gods", "the gods who live for ever" |

It is ἐόντες 'being', not a verb of living. The phrase names the gods by what men lack.

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| θεῶν ἐν γούνασι κεῖται (267) | "lie(s) on the knees of the gods" | same | "rests in the lap of the gods", "is up to the gods", "is in the hands of the gods" |

The image is kept literally in both layers. Its origin is disputed, and the note says so.

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| νηῦς θοή (260, 303) | "swift ship" | "swift ship" | "fast ship", "quick ship", "sharp ship" |

θοός is 'swift'. The rendering is generic and is recorded only so that it stays fixed.

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| κραναὴ Ἰθάκη (247) | "rocky Ithaca" | "rocky Ithaca" | "rugged", "craggy", "rock-strewn" |

κραναός means 'rocky, hard'. "Rocky" is the simplest word for it.

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ξανθὸς Μενέλαος (285) | "fair-haired Menelaus" | "fair-haired Menelaus" | "red-haired", "tawny", "golden-haired", "blond" |

ξανθός is a colour word, yellow to light brown. The English adds "haired", and the note says it does. "Tawny" is also avoided because the table already rules it out for αἴθων.

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ἀχαιοὶ χαλκοχίτωνες (286) | "the bronze-shirted Achaeans" | same | "bronze-armoured", "bronze-clad", "bronze-mailed" |

χιτών is a tunic. The English keeps the garment instead of widening it to armour in general.

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| Αἴγισθος δολόμητις (300) | "Aegisthus of guileful counsel" | same | "crafty", "treacherous", "wily" (too generic, and none of them shows μῆτις) |

δόλος + μῆτις. The rendering keeps both parts, and "guile" echoes δόλῳ at 296. It sits beside the table's "blameless" for ἀμύμων Αἴγισθος. The two are different epithets and are never merged.

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ἰσόθεος φώς (324) | "a man equal to a god" | "a man the equal of a god" | "godlike" (reserved for ἀντίθεος), "godlike in form" (θεοειδής), "a man like a god" |

ἴσος + θεός. It is the third "godlike" word in Book 1 so far, and like the others it is kept distinct.

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| κατὰ φρένα καὶ κατὰ θυμόν (294) | "in mind and in heart" | "in your/his mind and heart" | "in heart and soul", "in his inmost heart" |

φρένες is the seat of thought and θυμός the seat of feeling. Both are kept, in the Greek order.

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| εἰ δ’ ἄγε νῦν ξυνίει καὶ ἐμῶν ἐμπάζεο μύθων (271; second half = 305) | "Come now, then, attend, and take heed of my words" | "Come now, attend to me, and take heed of my words" | "mark my words", "listen well" |

It is a whole line, and its second half closes the speech at 305 in the same English ("take heed of my words").

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| πάντες κ’ ὠκύμοροί τε γενοίατο πικρόγαμοί τε (266) | "all of them would become swift-doomed and bitter-wedded" | "All of them would meet a swift doom and a bitter marriage" | "short-lived" (loses μόρος), "rue their wooing", "would all find …" (the verb and frame of the familiar published versions; changed at review) |

This whole-line curse on the suitors is likely to return. The literal layer keeps both compounds hyphenated.

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| Παναχαιοί (239) | "the Achaeans all together" | "all the Achaeans" | "the Panachaeans" (an English non-word) |

παν- + Ἀχαιοί.

## Names new to the poem in this part

Πηνελόπεια **Penelope** · Νέστωρ **Nestor** · Μενέλαος **Menelaus** · Ἶλος Μερμερίδης **Ilus son of Mermerus** ·
Ἐφύρη **Ephyra** · Δουλίχιον **Dulichium** · Σάμη **Same** · Ζάκυνθος **Zacynthus** · ἅρπυιαι **the Harpies**
(printed by the edition as a common noun; the English capitalises it and the note explains it as 'snatchers', the storm-winds).
Pylos and Sparta are already in odyssey-001 (1.93).
